title: Ecosystem signal chronicle and decision playbook for model-landscape shifts
creator: Asha Nair
description:
Goal: Build a repeatable, auditable chronicle of external model ecosystem signals and a lightweight decision playbook that PMs and GTM can use to prioritize sourcing, fallback and product adjustments.

Scope:
- Define the taxonomy of signals we will track (availability, latency regressions, pricing shocks, quantization adoption, license changes, upstream deprecations, provider outages, notable model feature launches).
- Design a time-series 'signal chronicle' that captures events, provenance, confidence score and downstream impact estimate (latency/cost/quality).
- Create a decision playbook with triage flows, escalation gates, and procurement/rollout recommendations tied to signal severity.
- Implement a minimal ingestion prototype (webhooks + manual curation) to capture 1 month of signals from public repos, vendor changelogs, Twitter threads, CI probes, and partner telemetry.
- Deliverables: signal taxonomy doc, signal chronicle CSV export, decision playbook markdown in Confluence, alerting knobs for existing Model Watch dashboards, and two sample triage decisions executed as case studies.

Success metrics:
- Signal chronicle contains >= 50 distinct events in first 30 days from at least 4 provenance sources.
- Decision playbook reduces time-to-decision for model-supply incidents from avg 72h to <= 24h in runbook simulation.
- PM/Eng triage playbook rated >= 4/5 in feasibility/usability survey from 6 internal stakeholders.

Stakeholders: PM (owner) - Asha Nair, Eng leads - Priya Rao and Mateo Alvarez (ingest prototype), Research - Dr. Noor Sheikh (signal weighting), Solutions/Sales - Jenna Morales (customer impact lens), Legal - TBC for licensing signal criteria.

Approach:
1) Rapid discovery (week 1): interview 8 internal stakeholders, audit current signal lists (Model Watch, Procurement), and finalize taxonomy.
2) Prototype ingestion (week 2): wire up 3 signal sources (GitHub releases, vendor status pages, monitoring probes) into a simple store; populate first 30-day chronicle.
3) Playbook drafting (week 2-3): convert triage flows into markdown, map to on-call rotations and escalation channels, add sample thresholds and runbook actions (notify Account Ops, trigger canary, enable quant fallback).
4) Validation (week 3-4): run 2 tabletop incidents, collect feedback, iterate.
5) Handoff (end of cycle): publish Confluence playbook, create dashboard cards and an initial alert rule in Signal Hub.

Data sources and artifacts:
- Confluence: /ModelIntelligence/SignalChronicle (placeholder link)
- Drive: SignalAtlas/Primitives.xlsx (prototype data dump)
- GitHub PR: redwood-internal/signal-ingest#42 (ingest prototype)
- Dashboards: analytics.redwood.com/dashboards/model-watch (to link alert rules)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: noisy signal ingestion will generate false positives. Mitigation: require multi-source corroboration and confidence scoring; start with manual curation.
- Risk: Legal concerns for vendor licensing signals. Mitigation: involve Legal in taxonomy review and strip proprietary content from public alerts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Taxonomy doc approved by Research and Legal.
- Prototype ingestion captures at least 3 distinct signal types and is running end-to-end in staging.
- Decision playbook includes at least 3 action pathways (low/medium/high severity) and 2 sample runbook executions recorded in the ticket.

Notes: this ticket is intended to create an operational primitive that can be iterated and automated in subsequent cycles (signal enrichment, ML ranking, automated mitigations).
